The two that matter: a HIGH tool always requires approval, and no tool may
accept a raw URL, a raw query or code. The second is why there is no generic
fetch tool - exfiltration through a tool argument needs somewhere to go.

props.doc:
THE governing function of the AI module.

Called at session start, before any incident text, alert body, email or
vendor response enters the context. The tool set is the intersection of the
registry, the permissions the invoking analyst actually holds, and the tool
set configured for this purpose - never a union, and never influenced by
anything the model reads.

That ordering is the structural defence against prompt injection: an
injected instruction cannot add a tool, because the model was never asked
which tools it wanted.
props.name: build_tool_set

props.code:
from soar.identity.rbac import has_permission

rows = db.query(
    "SELECT name, description, input_schema, output_schema, implementation, "
    "risk_level, required_permission, requires_approval, timeout_ms, "
    "max_calls_per_turn, scope "
    "FROM ai_tool WHERE enabled AND (org_id = %s OR org_id IS NULL) "
    "ORDER BY name", [principal["org_id"]], principal["org_id"],
)

held = principal.get("permissions") or []
allowed = [t for t in rows if has_permission(held, t["required_permission"])]

if purpose and purpose != "general":
    configured = db.query(
        "SELECT tool_name FROM ai_tool_set WHERE org_id = %s AND purpose = %s",
        [principal["org_id"], purpose], principal["org_id"],
    )
    names = {row["tool_name"] for row in configured}
    if names:
        allowed = [t for t in allowed if t["name"] in names]

return allowed

props.doc:
Five gates between a model asking for a tool and the tool running.

Schema, budget, scope, permission, approval. The scope gate is the one that
makes "isolate every host" inexpressible: the argument must name an entity
already attached to this incident, so constraining the SHAPE of an action
does the work that constraining its intent could never do reliably.

props.doc: The tools a fresh installation registers. Every one names a real command; none takes a URL, a query string or code.
props.name: builtin_tools

props.code:
def tool(name, description, implementation, inputs, risk, permission,
         scope="incident", approval=False, calls=10):
    return {
        "name": name, "description": description,
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "required": list(inputs.keys()),
                         "properties": inputs, "additionalProperties": False},
        "output_schema": {"type": "object"},
        "implementation": implementation,
        "risk_level": risk, "required_permission": permission,
        "requires_approval": approval or risk == "high",
        "timeout_ms": 30000, "max_calls_per_turn": calls, "scope": scope,
    }

indicator = {"indicator_id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^ind_[0-9A-Z]{26}$"}}
host = {"host_id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^host_[0-9A-Z]{26}$"}}

return [
    tool("lookup_indicator_reputation",
         "Look up the stored reputation and cached enrichment for one indicator "
         "already attached to this incident.",
         "command:intel.score", indicator, "low", "intel.read"),
    tool("enrich_indicator",
         "Run the IOC investigation playbook against one indicator on this "
         "incident and return the normalised verdict.",
         "playbook:ioc.investigation", indicator, "low", "playbooks.run"),
    tool("get_host_detail",
         "Retrieve endpoint detail from the EDR for a host already linked to "
         "this incident.",
         "command:crowdstrike.get_host", host, "low",
         "integrations.read"),
    tool("search_related_incidents",
         "Find other incidents in the last 30 days that share an entity or an "
         "indicator with this one.",
         "query:related_incidents", {}, "low", "incidents.read", scope="incident"),
    tool("search_siem",
         "Run a saved, parameterised SIEM query by name with a bounded time "
         "window. The query text comes from the saved query, not from this call.",
         "query:saved_siem",
         {"saved_query": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9_]{3,64}$"},
          "hours": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 168}},
         "low", "commands.execute", scope="global", calls=5),
    tool("add_incident_note",
         "Append an analyst-readable note to the incident timeline, attributed "
         "to the assistant.",
         "command:incident.note",
         {"text": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 4000}},
         "medium", "incidents.write"),
    tool("set_incident_severity",
         "Change the incident severity, with a stated rationale.",
         "command:incident.severity",
         {"severity": {"enum": ["info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical"]},
          "rationale": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 1000}},
         "medium", "incidents.write"),
    tool("create_investigation_task",
         "Create a task on this incident for a human to carry out.",
         "command:incident.task",
         {"title": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 200},
          "detail": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 2000}},
         "medium", "incidents.write"),
    tool("isolate_host",
         "Network-contain a host that is already an entity on this incident. "
         "Requires human approval, always.",
         "command:crowdstrike.isolate_host", host, "high",
         "response.isolate", approval=True, calls=3),
    tool("disable_account",
         "Disable an identity that is already an entity on this incident. "
         "Requires human approval, always.",
         "command:identity.disable",
         {"identity_id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^idn_[0-9A-Z]{26}$"}},
         "high", "response.disable_account", approval=True, calls=3),
]
